summary: Daniel Okonkwo, a 58-year-old man, was admitted on March 4, 2026 after five days of worsening shortness of breath on exertion, palpitations and one episode of chest tightness. He was diagnosed with new-onset atrial fibrillation with a fast heart rate and hypertensive urgency; acute coronary syndrome was ruled out. In hospital his heart rate was controlled and his blood pressure was brought down to a stable range. He also has hyperlipidemia, situational anxiety related to the new diagnoses, and mild GERD. He was discharged home in stable condition on March 11, 2026 with six medications: Velantine for hypertension, Cordizem-XR for rate control and hypertension, Pravoxil for hyperlipidemia, Etrazolam for acute anxiety, Pranixol for adjunctive cardiovascular protection, and Quintaxin for GERD prophylaxis. Follow-up is planned with primary care within seven days and cardiology within two weeks. Psychiatry follow-up is stated as within two weeks in one place and at the 8-week mark in another. A lipid panel is planned at six weeks and a basic metabolic panel at two weeks after discharge.
